name: Specification Coherence Review — Conflicts, Overlaps & Clarifications
description: For multi-standard design specifications (client spec + NORSOK/ISO/EN/class invocations). Extracts every requirement with a subject key, groups by subject across all provided documents, and detects: conflicts (same subject, incompatible values — both clauses cited), redundancies (most stringent noted), missing precedence order, and invoked-but-not-provided documents. Serves BOTH sides: the receiving engineer gets a ready-to-send technical query list; the issuing company runs it on drafts before sending. Conflict detection is pure code on the extraction (zero tokens). The engine flags candidates; engineering judgment disposes.

sections.title: Specification Overview & Document Set
sections.notes: 'provided_vs_invoked_split': every invoked document is marked PROVIDED (indexed) or NOT PROVIDED. Requirements can only be extracted from provided documents — an invoked-but-absent standard is itself a finding, honestly stated. Undated invocations flagged (edition ambiguity is a conflict seed).

sections.title: Order of Precedence

required_facts.label: Stated order of precedence between documents

sections.notes: THE most common root failure. If no precedence clause exists across the provided set → blocking gap: 'No order of precedence stated — every conflict below is unresolvable by the documents themselves.' If one exists, it is quoted verbatim and every conflict row references it.

sections.title: Requirements Register — Grouped by Subject
sections.notes: Extraction assigns each requirement a canonical subject key (design_life, ndt_extent, material_cert_level, weld_class, coating_system, safety_factor, testing_regime, documentation_language...). key = extracted_facts.key — the existing schema, no migration. Checkpoint: user confirms/merges subject grouping before conflict analysis (mis-grouped subjects create false conflicts). Modal precision preserved (shall/should/may never altered).

sections.title: Conflict & Overlap Register
sections.notes: PURE CODE on the confirmed register (zero tokens): group by subject key → compare values → classify: CONFLICT (incompatible values; both clauses verbatim side by side) | REDUNDANT (same demand from multiple sources; most stringent noted) | UNIQUE. Each conflict row: subject | doc A says (clause) | doc B says (clause) | precedence resolves? (from section 2) | disposition [engineer's column — the engine flags candidates, judgment disposes; a clause may apply to pressure parts only]. Severity: conflicts on mandatory requirements with no precedence = blocking.

sections.title: Technical Query / Clarification List
sections.notes: THE DELIVERABLE for the receiving engineer: one formally-worded query per unresolved conflict/gap, each citing both clauses verbatim and asking the issuer to state which governs. Optional '[AUTHOR: proposed resolution]' per query — proposing the answer speeds the client's reply. For the ISSUING side, this section renders instead as 'Fix before issue' with the same rows. Drafted, never sent — export and route through the project's formal TQ channel.

sections.title: Document & Clause Register
sections.notes: All provided documents with revision; invoked-but-not-provided documents listed as gaps.

sections.title: Declaration
sections.boilerplate: This review was compiled by extraction from the provided documents only; every requirement, conflict and gap is traceable to cited clauses. Conflicts are flagged as candidates by comparison of extracted values — their engineering and contractual significance must be assessed by qualified personnel. Documents invoked but not provided were not analysed. This is not legal or engineering advice.
sections.boilerplate_no: Denne gjennomgangen er sammenstilt ved uttrekk fra de fremlagte dokumentene alene; hvert krav, hver konflikt og hvert hull er sporbart til siterte klausuler. Konflikter er flagget som kandidater ved sammenligning av uttrukne verdier — deres faglige og kontraktsmessige betydning må vurderes av kvalifisert personell. Dokumenter som er påberopt men ikke fremlagt, er ikke analysert. Dette er ikke juridisk eller ingeniørfaglig rådgivning.
